mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly represents the lens formula for a thin lens?
mcqs.explanation: The standard lens formula for a thin lens, using the Cartesian sign convention, is 1/f = 1/v - 1/u, where f is the focal length, v is the image distance and u is the object distance. Option B states this correctly; the other options are incorrect forms.

mcqs.question: According to the Cartesian sign convention for lenses, which statement is true?

options.A: Object distance is taken as negative.
options.B: Image distance is positive only for virtual images.
options.C: Focal length of a convex (converging) lens is taken as positive.
options.D: All distances are taken as positive irrespective of direction.

mcqs.answer: Focal length of a convex (converging) lens is taken as positive.
mcqs.explanation: In the Cartesian sign convention, distances measured in the direction of incident light are taken as positive. For a convex (converging) lens, the focal length is positive. Option C reflects this rule. Option A is wrong because object distance is positive when the object is on the incoming side. Option B is wrong because image distance is positive for real images. Option D ignores sign conventions.

mcqs.question: The linear magnification (m) produced by a thin lens is defined as:

options.A: m = v / u (positive sign indicates an upright image)

mcqs.answer: m = v / u (positive sign indicates an upright image)
mcqs.explanation: Magnification m = image distance (v) divided by object distance (u). The sign of m tells the orientation: positive for upright, negative for inverted. Option A gives the correct definition. Options B, C, and D are incorrect forms.

mcqs.question: How is the optical power (P) of a thin lens defined?
mcqs.explanation: The power of a lens, measured in dioptres (D), is the reciprocal of its focal length expressed in metres: P = 1/f (m). Option B states this definition correctly. Options A, C, and D use incorrect relationships or units.

mcqs.question: A convex lens has a focal length of 0.25 m. What is its power in dioptres?
mcqs.explanation: Power P = 1/f. With f = 0.25 m, P = 1 ÷ 0.25 = 4 dioptres. The lens is converging, so the power is positive. Option B is correct; the other options are numerically incorrect or have the wrong sign.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand combination of lens powers at the required level
mcqs.question: Two thin lenses are placed in contact. Lens 1 has a power of +2 D and Lens 2 has a power of +3 D. What is the total power of the combination?
mcqs.explanation: When thin lenses are in contact, their powers add algebraically: P_total = P1 + P2 = +2 D + +3 D = +5 D. Option A reflects this. Options B, C, and D are incorrect sums or sign errors.

mcqs.question: Using the lens formula 1/f = 1/v – 1/u, if the object distance u = –30 cm and the image distance v = +60 cm, then the focal length f is –20 cm. Is this statement correct?

options.B: No, the focal length is +20 cm.
options.C: No, because the sign convention used is wrong.
options.D: It cannot be determined without additional information.

mcqs.answer: No, the focal length is +20 cm.
mcqs.explanation: Applying the formula: 1/f = 1/60 – 1/(–30) = 1/60 + 1/30 = 3/60 = 1/20, so f = +20 cm. The statement that f = –20 cm is incorrect. Option B correctly identifies the error. Option C is partially true but the main mistake is the sign of f, not the convention itself. Options A and D are wrong.

mcqs.question: An object is placed 15 cm in front of a convex lens of focal length +10 cm. Using the Cartesian sign convention, what is the sign and nature of the image distance?

options.B: Image distance = +30 cm, real inverted image.
options.C: Image distance = +30 cm, virtual upright image.

mcqs.answer: Image distance = +30 cm, real inverted image.
mcqs.explanation: Using 1/f = 1/v – 1/u with f = +10 cm, u = –15 cm (object on the incoming side): 1/10 = 1/v – 1/(–15) ⇒ 1/v = 1/10 – 1/15 = 1/30, so v = +30 cm. Positive v indicates a real image formed on the opposite side of the lens, which is inverted. Option B correctly states this. The other options give wrong signs or image nature.
